The LLC is the new one Blake and I are setting up for the three of us, and anything Harmony Games owns (the games with their art and listings, and the equipment) comes to it only through Sunset's sale, the way I wrote after the call on Wednesday. Services we keep running just move their billing to the LLC.\\nThe plan runs March 1 to May 31.\\nDomino Delights and Zombie Match come over only if what each made in January, going by the warehouse's daily revenue table, covers what its own hosting bills now, whatever we said about them before. {"documentId": "f_1e468a9d69ea0f0a2001f5", "title": "LLC ground rules (Combo Fighter and whatever else we take)", "name": "LLC ground rules (Combo Fighter and whatever else we take)", "revisionId": "89aa42aa1b", "createdTime": "2026-02-12T23:46:00Z", "modifiedTime": "2026-02-12T23:46:00Z", "text": "LLC ground rules (Combo Fighter and whatever else we take)
This is the lifestyle route I posted about in #executives. The LLC is the new one Blake and I are setting up for the three of us, and anything Harmony Games owns (the games with their art and listings, and the equipment) comes to it only through Sunset's sale, the way I wrote after the call on Wednesday. Services we keep running just move their billing to the LLC.
The plan runs March 1 to May 31.
Domino Delights and Zombie Match come over only if what each made in January, going by the warehouse's daily revenue table, covers what its own hosting bills now, whatever we said about them before. Combo Fighter comes over either way, it's the reason we're doing this. A game that comes over brings what it needs to keep running, its accounts and its player support.
Cost every item at what it bills now, going by whoever runs it, not by what HG used to pay.
What we already decided to keep or cancel for the shutdown in #winddown stays decided.
Pay for anyone who stays on is a separate conversation once we know the running cost; this plan is only what bills us every month, no one-offs or yearly fees.
How things move is on the LLC card on our board.
"}

Which competitors does this title sit next to?*\\nOn mobile, this title sits closest to:\\n\\u2022 The Sims (Freeplay / Mobile): deep life simulation and expression.\\n\\u2022 Cozy idle sims such as Cats & Soup and similar \\u201cwatch your world run\\u201d games.\\n\\u2022 Lifestyle and decor titles in the home design and fashion space.\\nThe key difference: we are effectively offering a \\u201cquick simulation\\u201d button for Barbie life moments. Every action is designed to resolve in short, satisfying sessions that fit mobile: start a career shift, run a mini day in Barbieland, complete a micro story, then step away.\\nWe borrow some loop structure from idle clickers to keep Barbie\\u2019s world running in the background, but unlike pure idle titles, this game adds roleplay, story context, and character identity on top of those systems. The result is closer to a \\u201csnackable Sims in Barbieland\\u201d than a standard clicker.\\n\\n*2. What gap in the market are you aiming to fill?*\\nThere is no mobile experience today that gives Barbie fans a living, evergreen Barbieland where they can:\\n\\u2022 Collect across the full, ever evolving Barbie universe, not just one product line.\\n\\u2022 Test drive careers, lifestyles, and aesthetics in a low friction, low cost way.\\n\\u2022 Return daily to see their Barbieland grow and change with the brand.\\nThe gap is a \\u201cBarbie lovers universe\\u201d that goes much deeper than a single dress up app or one Dreamhouse. This concept lets fans continuously engage with more facets of Barbie, and live those fantasies digitally at a fraction of the cost of physical collecting, while still driving demand for the physical line.\\n\\n*3. How does this differ from Dreamhouse Adventures, Miniverse, Toca Boca, etc.?*\\n\\u2022 *Dreamhouse Adventures:* Centered on one location and one core fantasy loop. Our concept treats the Dreamhouse as one important module inside a larger Barbieland, with careers, locations, and storylines that expand well beyond the house.\\n\\u2022 *Miniverse:* Focuses on miniature making and ASMR style crafting. We take some sensory inspiration, but our core is life simulation and roleplay: what Barbie does with those worlds once they exist.\\n\\u2022 *Toca Boca:* Fantastic at open ended play for kids, but genre agnostic and not rooted in Barbie\\u2019s IP or audience. We are designing a life sim where the mechanics, aesthetics, and progression are specifically tuned to Barbie\\u2019s brand promise and fanbase.\\nIn short, the IP to genre fit is unique. We are not putting Barbie on top of an existing mechanic. We are building systems that express what Barbie stands for in play: choice of path, creativity, and \\u201cyou can be anything.\\u201d\\n\\n*4. What is the aspirational hook that makes this uniquely Barbie?*\\nThe hook: \\u201cBuild your own Barbieland and live every \\u2018you can be anything\\u2019 fantasy inside it.\\u201d\\nA few pillars support that:\\n\\u2022 *More than one thing to do:* Players can move fluidly between careers, hobbies, fashion, travel, and social stories, just like kids do with the dolls.\\n\\u2022 *Modular and combinable:* Each play module (career tracks, locations, collections, events) snaps together, so your Barbieland feels personal and assembled, not scripted from a single storyline.\\n\\u2022 *Player chosen life paths:* The core loop reinforces the founding philosophy of Barbie: players project their own fantasy into the character and choose their own path, adventure, and profession.\\nThat combination of multi path aspiration plus real systems depth is something only Barbie can authentically own in this space.\\n\\n*5. How does this respond to current cozy sim and lifestyle trends?*\\nThe concept is built directly on top of what is working in cozy and lifestyle sims today:\\n\\u2022 Low pressure, low failure, high comfort play.\\n\\u2022 Strong focus on aesthetics, collection, and decoration that feels shareable and aspirational.\\n\\u2022 Light idle elements that reward coming back often without demanding long sessions.\\n\\u2022 High quality sensory feedback: soft animations, satisfying loops, ASMR like interactions.\\nWe then layer Barbie\\u2019s IP and audience targeting on top:\\n\\u2022 The fantasy and visual language map perfectly to the existing cozy and lifestyle audience, but filtered through Barbie\\u2019s world.\\n\\u2022 The brand gives us a more efficient route to the right players. With Barbie front and center, we can acquire fans at a lower CPI than a generic cozy sim, since the game speaks directly to a known, motivated segment.\\nIn effect, we take Proven cozy and idle patterns, align them tightly with Barbie\\u2019s brand promise, and use the IP to reach the exact audience that already craves this kind of experience.\", \"channel\": \"C09QDMC3UL9\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\", \"thread_ts\": \"1764867254.892579\"}, {\"ts\": \"1765213543.355689\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"*1. There is no mobile experience today that gives Barbie fans a living, evergreen Barbieland where they can:
• Collect across the full, ever evolving Barbie universe, not just one product line.
• Test drive careers, lifestyles, and aesthetics in a low friction, low cost way.

• *Dreamhouse Adventures:* Centered on one location and one core fantasy loop. Our concept treats the Dreamhouse as one important module inside a larger Barbieland, with careers, locations, and storylines that expand well beyond the house.

Went through every issue in the LLC project. My call is on each one, and the plan sheet is here (shared with you and Blake): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1KcyEpGC8UmDRDwbMVHUMPYoq4PtiGI63J-S4JOJwjXE/edit

What I'd do:
• **LLC takes CF and DD** through Sunset's sale. DD made $183.11 in January (warehouse daily revenue table), which covers the $140/mo its prod account bills now, so it comes over. ZM made $0, so ZM and its AWS account stay with HG.
• **Billing moves to the LLC by Mar 1:** DD prod AWS $140, CF backend/auth $62 (Blake got it down from $95). AppsFlyer free tier for CF, $0.
• **Blake already pays himself through May:** Metabase $100, dbt $100, GitHub $48 = $248. Those count toward his third.
• **Everything else stays with HG:** Singular, Figma (prepaid to Sep, so not LLC like the draft had it), Unity Pro (CF is fine on Personal), Slack/Google/Linear/Deel/Gusto/Intuit/Carta, build boxes, the cancelled tools, the Apple and Play accounts, the playable one-off. Calm Play isn't used, since the LLC is the new one you and Blake are setting up.
• **One snag:** Apple rejected DD on Friday because in-app support only opens an email draft. ENG-2462 is back in Todo for Blake to add a support URL.

**Cost, March through May:** $450 a month all in ($202 billed to the LLC plus Blake's $248), so **$150 each per month**. You and I each put in $150 cash. Blake puts in $0 because his $248 already covers his third, and the LLC pays him back the extra $98 a month.

content.text:
Your answer is ready for Monday: the plan sheet is in your Drive, every Linear issue has your call on it, and I've replied in Leonard's thread with the sheet link. It costs each of you **$150 a month** from March through May.

**What I decided, using his ground rules doc:**
- **Combo Fighter and Domino Delights come to the LLC** through Sunset's sale. DD made $183.11 in January, according to the warehouse's daily revenue table. That covers the $140 a month its AWS hosting now bills, so it comes over.
- **Zombie Match stays with HG.** It made $0 in January and its AWS account still bills every month.
- **Monthly costs:**
  - The LLC pays DD's AWS ($140) and Combo Fighter's AWS ($62). Blake cut CF's from $95 on Thursday night.
  - AppsFlyer replaces Singular for CF on its free tier, so $0.
  - Blake already pays GitHub ($48), dbt ($100) and Metabase ($100) on his own card through May. That's $248, and it counts toward his share.
- **Everything else stays with HG.** That includes Figma, which Leonard's Tuesday draft had going to the LLC. HG prepaid it to September 11, so the LLC has nothing to pay. I also didn't use Calm Play LLC: the ground rules say the LLC is the new one Leonard and Blake are setting up.

**Money:** the total is $450 a month, so each third is $150. You and Leonard each put in $150 cash. Blake puts in nothing because his $248 already covers his third, and the LLC pays him back the extra $98 a month.

**One thing still open:** Apple rejected Domino Delights on Thursday night because its only in-app support is an email draft. I reopened the player support issue (ENG-2462) and assigned it to Blake to add a support link by March 1. My Slack reply says Apple rejected it "on Friday"; that's the UTC date, it was Thursday night your time.

**Linear now matches the sheet:**
- **To do (6):**
  - You: buy Combo Fighter through Sunset's sale.
  - Leonard: buy Domino Delights through the sale, and set up AppsFlyer.
  - Blake: move both AWS accounts to the LLC, and fix DD support.
- **Done (3):** the three Blake pays himself.
- **Canceled (28):** everything that stays with HG.

Files are in your Drive:
- LLC 90 days (plan)
